title: Boltzmann Brains & Poincaré Recurrence
description: A dead universe is not quite dead. In a finite system at equilibrium every state comes back, given time, and fluctuations out of equilibrium happen by pure chance - a star, a planet, a brain. Unlocks the Boltzmann Fluctuation.

puzzle.goal: A small part of a universe at equilibrium, at temperature T, can fluctuate by chance into a state with a little more energy (by Δ_E) and a little less entropy (by Δ_S) than it should have. The probability falls off exponentially in the free energy the fluctuation needs, measured in units of k_BT. Write the probability.
puzzle.name: Einstein–Boltzmann fluctuation formula
puzzle.form: exp ( - ( Δ _ E - T * Δ _ S ) / ( kB * T ) )
puzzle.ask: A brain-sized fluctuation that costs no energy but lowers the entropy by S × 10⁵⁰ k_B has 1/P = 10^X. Find X in units of 10⁵⁰. (A whole universe returns, by Poincaré recurrence, after about e^{10¹²²} years - far longer.)
puzzle.method: Einstein's fluctuation formula: the probability of a state is e^{S/k_B}; for a subsystem in contact with a bath use the total entropy change, Δ_S − Δ_E/T.
